entry.title: Telemetry v2: explicit choices, every round reported, real opt-out, n…
entry.content:
Telemetry v2: explicit choices, every round reported, real opt-out, no keys in git (#1012)

* Telemetry v2: client header, round and pool revision on the choice ping, picker capture

- Every /api/roll and /api/chosen request sends X-Impeccable-Client:
  impeccable/<skill version, else engine+engine>[ <channel>], with the
  channel from IMPECCABLE_TELEMETRY_CHANNEL (test in tests and CI).
- API rolls record poolRevision, source, mode and register in roll.json,
  and every API-dealt round enters a per-key seed ledger under
  .impeccable/questions/seeds/ that outlives the decision page.
- The /api/chosen body gains reroll, poolRevision and source. The agent
  ping fills them from the ledger, drops a chosenId that is not a dealt
  catalog id of that round (the kind still goes), and accepts --reroll;
  the TELEMETRY line passes --reroll on re-roll rounds.
- The decision page sends the ping itself (source picker) when the card
  kind is certain: canon, a verdict card matching exactly one dealt world,
  and on plain rounds the pick kicker and the assigned lead. It marks the
  round before writing the answer, so the agent rerun prints
  "choice already recorded"; a failed send clears the mark.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Telemetry v2: explicit card identity, every round reported, runtime state kept out of git

Card identity and capture:
- Decision-page options on direction and surface rounds (payloads with
  buildPath) declare kind (assigned, pick, challenger, dealt) and, on
  challengers, catalogId; --start and --update refuse the payload until
  they do and check catalogId against the dealt worlds. Schema, schema
  note, new-work.md, and the contract document the fields.
- The picker sends what the card declares (kindSource explicit), on
  safer and bolder rounds too, falls back to the old kicker and verdict
  conventions only for cards without a kind (kindSource inferred), and
  carries option, the chosen card's position, on every card ping.
- Re-roll answers send kind reroll with the steer as register and the
  rejected round; surface rounds send scope surface, assigned for the
  dealt lead, challenger with its catalog id, and option alone for the
  other dealt structures.
- The agent path accepts --kind reroll and --option <n>; the TELEMETRY
  line names the flags per scope and the re-roll report.

Privacy:
- Every write under .impeccable/questions/ keeps a self-ignoring
  .gitignore there; the kept world card copies and build state.json get
  the same treatment, so a committed roll record can no longer tie
  telemetry to a repository.
- The seed ledger is named by a hash of the key and stores neither the
  key nor timestamps; roll.json's at is floored to the minute.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Telemetry v2: seed reference in committed files, opt-out reaches the server, handId

- concept-seed prints SEED REFERENCE (seed: plus 16 hex of SHA-256 of
  "impeccable-seed:" + key) for the surface brief and build-phase, and
  --from (and IMPECCABLE_CONCEPT_SEED) resolves a reference through the
  local, ignored seed ledger, so rolls, re-rolls, reproduced deals and the
  choice ping keep the real key without it ever being committed. An
  unknown reference is refused with the way out. build-phase stores the
  reference for --direction. new-work.md and visualize.md record the
  reference, never the key.
- Opt-out: DO_NOT_TRACK / IMPECCABLE_NO_TELEMETRY count when non-empty and
  not 0 or false; "telemetry": false in ~/.impeccable/config.json (written
  by the new `impeccable telemetry off|on|status`) or the project config
  also counts. Opted out, the roll still runs and sends
  X-Impeccable-Telemetry: off, no ping is sent, and no telemetry field or
  sent mark is stored.
- /api/roll's handId (32 lowercase hex) is stored per round and sent in
  every /api/chosen body for that round.
- README gains a Telemetry section; the contract, CLAUDE.md, oracle
  goldens and DELTAS.md follow.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Telemetry v2: address PR review (tracked files, salted references, ledger lock, pending pings)

- Tracked runtime files: a one-time TRACKED RUNTIME FILES notice (one
  git ls-files, only inside a work tree, never fatal) with the exact
  `git rm -r --cached` fix; while roll.json is tracked the record goes to
  the untracked roll.local.json. Docs no longer claim nothing can reach a
  commit.
- New roll keys are 128 bits from the OS CSPRNG. Seed references are
  salted per user (~/.impeccable/seed-salt), so they can be neither
  enumerated nor computed from a key in the telemetry dataset; the roll
  record stores the reference and no time (age is its mtime).
- The ignore file is written before roll.json.
- Ledger updates run under a per-file lock (create-new, stale takeover)
  with unique temp names.
- The page claims a round as pending; the agent rerun waits for it and
  sends itself when the send failed or is still pending past the
  deadline. Both sends carry the round's random pingId for server dedupe.
- Project opt-out is read at cwd, project root and repo root.
- `telemetry off|on` never overwrites a malformed user config.
- New card kind `grounded` (any number), sent as the ping kind.
- Pruning keeps the key behind a reference.
- question-update-comps-next declares kinds and is checked again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Telemetry v2: second review round (no unsalted references, pingId-scoped completions)

- No valid persisted salt (unwritable home and project, or a corrupt salt
  file, which is never rewritten) means no seed reference at all: the
  roll prints SEED REFERENCE unavailable and asks for `seed: none
  (unavailable)`, the roll record names no seed, and build-phase stores
  `none`. A read-only home falls back to the project's ignored
  .impeccable/questions/seed-salt.
- Ledger completions (confirm/release) carry the sent pingId and change
  nothing when the round now names another report.
- Pruning re-checks the file's age and skips pending rounds under the lock.
- The test channel is set after the inherited env in the engine-bin
  helper, the skill-behavior harness and the oracle.
- The finish reviewer and new-work.md require the SEED REFERENCE,
  corroborated against the roll output or `concept-seed --check-seed`,
  and accept `seed: none (unavailable)` only where no salt exists; a raw
  key in FORM is a material fix.
- Opt-out reasons and config errors print forward-slash paths on Windows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Seed salts: an existing salt always wins, references resolve under every salt

A sandboxed run with a read-only home made a project salt; once the home
became writable, salt() created a new home salt and the earlier
references stopped resolving. Now an existing valid salt (home, then
project) always wins over creating one, and Ledger::resolve (so --from and
--check-seed) accepts a reference made under any valid salt the machine
keeps.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Seed ledger: one locator across every kept salt

resolve() accepted references under any kept salt, but round(), claim(),
confirm(), release(), record_*() and prune went to the file named by the
primary salt only, so after a home salt appeared beside a project salt a
sandbox roll's rounds were invisible: the page could not claim and the
agent lost the pingId, hand and sent mark. Ledger::file now returns the
first existing file among the key's names under every kept salt, falling
back to the primary salt's name only for a new ledger, and every
operation goes through it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Seed ledger: tolerate Windows lock and rename contention

On Windows a create racing the delete of the same lock name fails with
access denied, not exists, and a rename over a file another thread has
open can fail for a moment. The lock now treats both as contention and
waits, and the ledger write retries its rename briefly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Seed ledger: a key's salt is chosen once and everything derives from it

The printed reference still came from the primary salt while the ledger
was found under the salt the key was first rolled with, so after a salt
switch a re-roll printed and stored a reference this machine could not
resolve. One shared locator (impeccable_common::seed::locate) now answers
for a key: its existing ledger wherever it is (names under every kept
salt, then a folder scan for a salt now out of reach), whose reference is
its own file name; only a key with no ledger takes the primary salt. The
printed SEED REFERENCE, the roll record, every ledger operation, --from,
--check-seed and build-phase --direction all derive from that answer, and
a reference resolves by the file it names. A ledger made with no salt is
marked unsalted and yields no reference.

The ledger lock checks its deadline on every pass, the stale branch
included, so an undeletable lock gives up instead of spinning.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Seed ledger: legacy no-salt names stay unsalted; fresh keys skip the search

A ledger named by the no-salt tag but written before the "unsalted"
marker existed is now treated as unsalted, so its name never becomes a
committable reference or resolves. A key the engine just generated has no
ledger anywhere, so it takes the primary salt without a name check or
folder scan; supplied keys and re-rolls still go through the search.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Draw code-led decision cards as HTML sketches in a skeleton treatment…
entry.content:
Draw code-led decision cards as HTML sketches in a skeleton treatment (#997)

* Draw code-led decision cards as HTML sketches in a skeleton treatment

A card may declare html, one first-viewport HTML file the agent writes after
serving. serve-question serves it at /sketch/<n> with a skeleton pass injected
(text under 22px becomes bars), tracks it per hand like comps so a re-roll
never shows the last hand's file, opens the raw file from the expand chip,
and carries it in ANSWER with a CHOSEN SKETCH line. concept-seed's code-led
and image-less PRESENTATION lines ask for one sketch per card and wait until
they land. The wireframe stays the fallback.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Address review: sandbox sketches, gate the chosen sketch, frames, write-time provenance

- /sketch/<n> carries a CSP that sandboxes the file and closes every network
  path but fonts; the raw view runs no script.
- The answer carries html only for this hand's sketch on a card the comp face
  did not replace, so CHOSEN SKETCH never contradicts a comp or names a
  leftover file.
- A hand records startedAt and its sketches: a sketch written after the hand
  began counts even with identical bytes, and --wait names stale ones.
- htmlFrame lets a phone or native surface sketch its own first screen; the
  slot follows the frame and turns portrait.
- The surface roll body asks for sketches, not wireframes.
- Two browser tests cover arrival, skeleton, staleness, raw view, the pick
  and a comp flip.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Flip back to code restores the sketch over a landed comp

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Operate and Read surfaces are code-led whatever build path is recorde…
entry.content:
Operate and Read surfaces are code-led whatever build path is recorded (#990)

* Operate and Read surfaces are code-led whatever build path is recorded

In blind ratings, image comps of working screens and documents scored
2.0 to 2.9 across five rule changes, while code-led builds of the same
briefs scored 3 to 3.5 and were always complete. So the build path is now
decided per mode: concept-seed --mode operate|read prints the code-led
PRESENTATION lines and a code buildPath for the payload, whatever the
project recorded. The recorded default, and the comp default when
nothing is recorded, govern Persuade and Experience only. The decision
page keeps its toggle, so one round can still be flipped to comp; a flip
on these surfaces is never offered for recording.

new-work.md retires 'not a per-surface decision'; init's question says
what the choice covers; the boot directive says the same.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Scope the recorded build path to Persuade and Experience everywhere it is described

Review findings on the code-led default: the BUILD_PATH_DEFAULT directive, the
surface roll body, the structured-tool fallback, the unset-buildPath staleness
finding, doctor.md and the README still described the recorded value as
governing every round. Also restores the MODE RULES doc comment to
mode_rules_block.

entry.title: live: keep the Astro carbonize style block is:inline (#993)
entry.content:
live: keep the Astro carbonize style block is:inline (#993)

On accept, the carbonize block was written with a bare <style> on every
non-JSX file. In an .astro file that is not the same thing as the
is:inline tag the variants block used: Astro compiles it into a
?astro&type=style&index=N module ahead of the page's own, and the
carbonize cleanup then deletes it again together with a markup change.

Astro 7.3.6 (withastro/astro#18076) drops its compile metadata on such a
save, so the reload of the index that vanished fails with "No Astro CSS
at index 1": a 500 in the dev server and two errors in the browser
console after every accept that carries CSS. On 7.3.5 and earlier the
same sequence logged nothing but served stale CSS under the surviving
index.

The carbonize block now takes the file type's own styleTag, so on Astro
it stays is:inline and the set of compiled style modules never changes
during a session. Output for every other file type is byte-identical.

The astro-vite7 live-e2e fixture goes back to a floating ^7.1.0 (it was
pinned to 7.3.5 to unblock a release). New oracle cases
live-accept-astro-variant-2-steps and live-accept-astro-discard were
recorded from the binary; no existing golden changed.

Fixes #992

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Dom trait reads an image's load state (#981)
entry.content:
Dom trait reads an image's load state (#981)

* Dom trait reads an image's load state

A rule pack could not tell a loaded image from one whose source failed:
the snapshot records naturalWidth and currentSrc for the visual pass, but
the Dom trait had no way to read them.

Three methods, each defaulting to None so existing DOMs and packs are
unaffected: image_natural_size, image_complete and image_current_src.
They answer for an HTML img only. SnapshotDom reads the media record the
capture already writes; the snapshot now also records `complete` for an
img (`md.cp`), and a capture recorded before that reads as None, never
false. FakeDom carries the three as fields, and the in-page probe reads
them off the element.

No built-in rule calls them, so built-in output is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01NVRDkUjxSbedQmcoEeQFq5

* Check the image load state against a rendered page

The snapshot test builds its media record by hand, so nothing checked that
the capture writes `complete` or that the in-page probe answers the same
way. This renders a loaded image, one whose source is a 404, a picture
whose chosen source is a 404, an unrequested lazy image, an
`input type=image` and a div in an installed browser, and compares the
probe's answers with the capture's.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01NVRDkUjxSbedQmcoEeQFq5

* Say what natural size and complete each report; cover SVG image

The natural size is known as soon as the browser has read the image's
dimensions, which can be before the fetch ends, and `complete` reports
that the request is over, not that an image came of it. The docs read as
if each were a decode status; they now say what each reports and that a
failed image is the combination.

The rendered-page test also asks an SVG `image`, which answers None from
both the probe and the capture.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01NVRDkUjxSbedQmcoEeQFq5
